description: CLEAN SLATE TRAINING - Optimized loss weights for thin stroke preservation based on dataset analysis (44.14% thin strokes available). CRITICAL FIX: pixel_loss 50→100 (+2x), adv_loss 3.0→1.0 (-3x), perceptual 1.0→2.0 (+2x). Target: >75% thin stroke preservation while maintaining PSNR≥16dB and F-Measure≥98%.
_comment_loss_weights: CRITICAL CHANGES for thin stroke preservation:
_rationale_pixel: pixel 50→100: Force generator to preserve ALL pixels including thin strokes
_rationale_adv: adv 3.0→1.0: Reduce discriminator aggression (was treating thin strokes as noise)
_rationale_perceptual: perceptual 1.0→2.0: Maintain structure quality while preserving fine details
_rationale_rec_feat: rec_feat 8.0 unchanged: Keep HTR guidance stable (proven effective)
_rationale_ctc: ctc 0.15 unchanged: Keep text recognition guidance stable

experiment_metadata.hypothesis: Dataset has 44.14% thin strokes but production_v3 lost 56.6% of them due to adversarial loss too high (3.0). Training from scratch with balanced losses (pixel=100, adv=1.0, perceptual=2.0) should preserve >75% thin strokes while maintaining quality metrics.
experiment_metadata.success_criteria: Thin stroke preservation 43.4% → >75% while maintaining PSNR ≥16 dB and F-Measure ≥98%
experiment_metadata.rationale: Clean slate training is OPTIMAL because: (1) Dataset already has sufficient thin strokes (44.14%), (2) Optimizer starts fresh with correct objective, (3) Model learns proper balance from epoch 0, (4) No conflicting gradients from previous training

dataset_analysis.conclusion: Sufficient thin stroke representation - problem is in loss weights, not data

problem_diagnosis.root_cause: adv_loss_weight=3.0 too aggressive - discriminator penalizes thin strokes as noise
problem_diagnosis.solution: Rebalance: pixel↑ (preserve detail), adv↓ (reduce aggression), perceptual↑ (maintain structure)
